title: Sysmon Run and RunOnce Registry Value Sets
exclusions: Reports Microsoft Sysmon Event ID 13 `SetValue` observations at the four Microsoft-documented machine/per-user Run and RunOnce locations and their 32-bit `Wow6432Node` views. It does not cover Startup folders, Policies Explorer Run, RunServices, StartupApproved, Winlogon, Active Setup, services, tasks, WMI, key creation/deletion/rename, or native Security Event ID 4657. A value-set event does not prove the command executed, persisted, was malicious, or remains present. Microsoft documents complete written-value recording for DWORD/QWORD; `Details` must not be assumed to contain every string command on every Sysmon schema. Per-user paths appear as `HKU\<SID>`, not `HKCU`. The five-minute cadence, five-minute ingestion allowance, one-result trigger, routing, retention, and exceptions are local choices. This rule performs no deletion, isolation, blocking, or compliance attestation.
evidence: After deployment, retain the approved Sysmon binary/version and configuration hash; effective RegistryEvent and XML input configuration; Splunk Add-on for Sysmon version; endpoint/source-health and field-quality results; `windows_sysmon_run_runonce_value_sets` saved-search definition, ACL, schedule, dispatch, and alert history; each result and raw XML; current-state registry query; correlated process/logon/software-deployment evidence; disposition; bounded exception match; and dated positive, negative, boundary, duplicate, delayed, extraction-loss, and recovery tests. This documentation-only review created no registry value, endpoint event, saved search, alert, dashboard, or production evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated index and fixed dispatch interval, replay authentic-shaped Sysmon XML EventCode 13 with `EventType=SetValue`, `TargetObject=HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\UC12119Test`, `Image=C:\Windows\System32\reg.exe`, distinct ProcessGuid, ProcessId, User, Details, Computer, EventRecordID, `_time`, and `_indextime`. Expect exactly one row with `scope=machine`, `registry_key=HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run`, `value_name=UC12119Test`, preserved process/value/event identity, and `use_case=UC-1.2.119`. Repeat with `HKU\S-1-5-21-111-222-333-1107\Software\Wow6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce\UC12119UserTest`; expect one `scope=user` row.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay otherwise equivalent EventCode 12 and 14 records; EventCode 13 at `RunServices`, `Policies\Explorer\Run`, `Explorer\StartupApproved\Run`, or a Run key with no value-name component; EventCode 13 from another source; an out-of-window event; and a record without endpoint identity. Expect zero rows for each. Replay EventCode 13 with missing Details, Image, User, or EventRecordID and expect a retained row with explicit `unknown` rather than silent suppression. Prove an exact, unexpired endpoint/key/value/process exception affects downstream notification only; wildcard, actor-only, expired, and source-health exceptions must not hide the base row.

dataSources: Microsoft Sysmon Event ID 13 (`RegistryEvent` value set) from `Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > Sysmon > Operational`, collected as XML to deployment-chosen `index=windows`, `source=XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational`, `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`. Required fields are `_time`, `_indextime`, `host`/`Computer`, `source`, `sourcetype`, `EventCode`, `EventType`, `TargetObject`, `Image`, `ProcessGuid`, `ProcessId`, `User`, `Details`, and `EventRecordID`. The deployed Sysmon RegistryEvent filter must include the exact Run/RunOnce paths; absence of events is not proof of coverage.
app: Splunk Add-on for Sysmon (`Splunk_TA_microsoft_sysmon`, Splunkbase 5709) 5.0.1 supplies the supported Sysmon input and search-time field/CIM knowledge for Splunk Platform 9.2+ and Sysmon 15.0. A deployment app owns the endpoint configuration, input, source-health search, saved search, dashboard, fixtures, and bounded exception lookup. No premium Splunk app is required for the raw detector.
spl:
index=windows sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog source="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=13 earliest=-10m@m latest=-5m@m
| eval endpoint=lower(trim(coalesce(Computer,dest,host))), event_type=lower(trim(coalesce(EventType,"unknown"))), target_object=coalesce(TargetObject,""), process_path=coalesce(Image,"unknown"), process_guid=coalesce(ProcessGuid,"unknown"), process_id=coalesce(ProcessId,"unknown"), registry_user=coalesce(User,user,"unknown"), observed_value=coalesce(Details,"unknown"), event_record_id=coalesce(EventRecordID,RecordNumber,"unknown")
| eval registry_key=replace(target_object,"\\[^\\]+$",""), value_name=replace(target_object,"^.*\\",""), registry_key_lc=lower(registry_key), scope=case(match(registry_key_lc,"^hklm\\"),"machine",match(registry_key_lc,"^hku\\[^\\]+\\"),"user",true(),"unknown")
| eval relative_key=replace(registry_key_lc,"^(hklm|hku\\[^\\]+)\\","")
| where event_type="setvalue" AND scope!="unknown" AND relative_key IN ("software\\microsoft\\windows\\currentversion\\run","software\\microsoft\\windows\\currentversion\\runonce","software\\wow6432node\\microsoft\\windows\\currentversion\\run","software\\wow6432node\\microsoft\\windows\\currentversion\\runonce") AND len(endpoint)>0 AND len(value_name)>0
| eval event_time=strftime(_time,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), indexed_time=strftime(_indextime,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"), use_case="UC-1.2.119"
| table _time event_time indexed_time endpoint scope registry_key value_name observed_value process_path process_guid process_id registry_user event_type event_record_id source sourcetype use_case
| sort 0 -_time endpoint registry_key value_name
description: Reports one row per Sysmon Event ID 13 value-set observation at an exact machine or per-user Run/RunOnce autostart key, including 32-bit views, during the completed dispatch slice. Each row preserves key/value identity, observed value detail, writer process and user, event record, event/index times, and source; missing optional evidence remains visible as `unknown`.
value: Run and RunOnce values can start software at sign-in, so an unexpected write can create durable security and support risk. Precise path boundaries and process-aware evidence accelerate triage against software deployment, user profile, current registry state, and later execution while avoiding misclassification of adjacent keys or every installer action as malicious.
implementation: Deploy and qualify Sysmon 15.0 with reviewed RegistryEvent includes for the exact Run/RunOnce paths, collect its Operational channel as XML with Splunk Add-on for Sysmon 5.0.1, and verify field/source health. Save the supplied SPL as `windows_sysmon_run_runonce_value_sets`, run every five minutes over the preceding complete slice after five minutes of measured ingestion allowance, and trigger on any result. Investigate current value, writer process, account, software/change context, and later execution before assigning severity; apply only exact expiring notification exceptions after preserving the result.
visualization: Dashboard `Windows — Run and RunOnce Value Sets`: put expected-endpoint Sysmon/config/source health first, followed by a newest-first table of endpoint, machine/user scope, key, value name/detail, process, user, event/index time, record ID, owner, and disposition. Add a 24-hour timeline, 30-day key/value/process prevalence, newly seen tuples, and raw XML/current-state drilldowns. Display `Details=unknown` as evidence loss, not a blank command, and never present no Event ID 13 rows as proof that no autostart values exist.
cimSpl:
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where (Registry.registry_path="*\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run*" OR Registry.registry_path="*\\Wow6432Node\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run*") by Registry.action Registry.dest Registry.process_guid Registry.process_id Registry.registry_hive Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_data Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_type Registry.user Registry.vendor_product
| rename Registry.* as *
| eval registry_path_lc=lower(registry_path)
| where match(registry_path_lc,"\\(wow6432node\\)?microsoft\\windows\\currentversion\\run(once)?(\\|$)")
| table firstTime lastTime count action dest process_guid process_id registry_hive registry_path registry_value_name registry_value_data registry_value_type user vendor_product
| sort 0 -lastTime
schema: Native Microsoft Sysmon Event ID 13 XML; optional CIM Endpoint.Registry
dataModelAcceleration: Optional only after raw-to-CIM parity testing. Splunk Security Content uses `Endpoint.Registry` for its registry-persistence analytic, but a normalized dataset can include other products/actions and does not guarantee raw EventType, EventRecordID, source identity, or Sysmon `Details` semantics. Validate tags, acceleration range/lag, exact path boundaries, writer fields, unknown-value retention, and source-health visibility. The raw Event ID 13 SPL remains the evidentiary detector.

knownFalsePositives:
A returned row is a real Sysmon value-set observation; the false positive is the downstream conclusion that every write is unauthorized persistence.

1. **Application install, update, repair, or removal** — Collaboration clients, tray utilities, endpoint products, and update agents can create or replace Run values. Match endpoint, exact key/value/data, signed package/writer evidence, deployment job, target ring, and approved UTC window. A publisher or `Program Files` path alone is insufficient.

2. **Windows/device setup and first user sign-in** — Provisioning and drivers can use RunOnce to complete setup. Verify image/build, device package, user SID/profile creation, expected one-time value, and disappearance after successful completion. Repeated recreation remains reviewable.

3. **Endpoint management, security, VPN, backup, or support agent** — Managed tools may enforce an autostart value. Require a version-controlled baseline for exact key/value/data/process and software owner. Changed command data, process, endpoint class, or timing must not inherit approval.

4. **Group Policy Preferences or configuration-management remediation** — Central automation may rewrite an approved value on drift. Correlate policy/job ID, targeted collection, service account/process, desired value, and run history. Never allow-list all writes by SYSTEM, PowerShell, `reg.exe`, or a management account.

5. **Administrator troubleshooting or incident response** — An operator can add, repair, or remove a startup value under a ticket. Preserve the row, exact action, current state, operator/logon evidence, host, value, and bounded authorization; administrator status is not approval.

6. **Authorized red-team or control test** — A T1547.001 test intentionally writes a Run value. Match exercise ID, named operator, exact hosts/values, exclusive start/end, expected process, and cleanup proof. Retain result and alert evidence.

7. **Duplicate direct plus WEC collection or replay** — Compare originating computer, channel, EventRecordID, `_raw`, and `_indextime`. Repair collection ownership/checkpoint state; do not broadly `dedup` by key/value because rapid repeated writes can be real.

**Safe notification suppression:** apply `windows_run_runonce_exceptions.csv` only after the base result, keyed by exact lowercase endpoint, normalized full registry key, value name, expected value hash/pattern, process path/hash where available, numeric `valid_from`/exclusive `valid_until`, owner, approver, ticket, and reason. Reject wildcard keys, host-only/process-only/actor-only matches, open-ended rows, and exceptions for missing source health or required extraction. Preserve the original row and matched exception for audit.
hardware: In-scope Windows clients and servers with Microsoft Sysmon 15.0 installed, running, and configured to include exact machine and loaded-user Run/RunOnce RegistryEvent paths. Endpoints without Sysmon, unloaded/offline user profiles, writes filtered before collection, values predating retention, and non-registry startup mechanisms require separate coverage.
reviewer: documentation-only editorial review against primary Microsoft Sysmon Event ID 13 and Run/RunOnce documentation, current Splunk Add-on for Sysmon and Splunk Security Content documentation, and MITRE ATT&CK; no registry write, Sysmon deployment/configuration, XML event, field extraction, SPL/CIM execution, fixture replay, exception, alert delivery, dashboard, endpoint response, scale test, or Microsoft/Splunk/endpoint-security SME runtime sign-off

cost.search_load_notes: The saved search selects one Event ID and four exact path families over one completed five-minute slice. Shared storage cost depends on the broader Sysmon RegistryEvent configuration; broad unfiltered registry collection can be high volume.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and exact contract

Assign Windows endpoint, Sysmon configuration, Splunk collection/content, software deployment, identity/profile, source-health, and incident-response owners. Inventory in-scope endpoints, loaded user profiles, Sysmon/service/configuration version, direct-forwarder or WEF/WEC route, software baselines, and responsible teams. Install Microsoft Sysmon 15.0 through normal change control and Splunk Add-on for Sysmon 5.0.1 on the tiers required by its guide; qualify the exact Windows, Sysmon, universal-forwarder, add-on, CIM, indexer, search-head, and Splunk Cloud versions in nonproduction.

Microsoft documents four principal locations: machine and current-user `Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run` and `RunOnce`. Sysmon represents user hives as `HKU\<SID>` and abbreviates machine root as `HKLM`. This contract adds the corresponding `Software\Wow6432Node` views but deliberately excludes similarly named persistence keys. Exactly one Event ID 13 `SetValue` at one in-scope value path produces one row. There is no count threshold: one unauthorized write matters, while many approved rollout writes can be benign. Classification depends on authorization and context.

Sysmon says Event ID 13 identifies registry value modifications and explicitly documents recording the written value for DWORD/QWORD. Do not promise that `Details` is complete command data for every string/value/schema combination. The event identifies a write, not later sign-in execution or current state.

## Step 1 — Configure endpoint and Splunk collection

Merge narrow RegistryEvent includes into the organization's reviewed Sysmon configuration. Use the schema accepted by the deployed binary and test ordering/group relations; do not replace a mature policy with an internet template. Representative path conditions include `\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\`, `RunOnce\`, and both `\Software\Wow6432Node\...` equivalents. Record the active configuration hash, use Sysmon's `-c` update path under change control, and inspect Event ID 16 for configuration changes and Event ID 255 for errors. Confirm the Operational channel locally before blaming Splunk.

Collect XML through an app-owned `local/inputs.conf` stanza:

```ini
[WinEventLog://Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational]
disabled = 0
renderXml = true
index = windows
checkpointInterval = 5
```

The index is deployment-owned. The add-on documents `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`; preserve channel identity as `source=XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational`. Do not edit an add-on's `default` directory. If WEF/WEC is used, follow the add-on's dedicated collector guidance, preserve originating `Computer` as endpoint, measure subscription latency, and prevent simultaneous endpoint plus collector ingestion.

Inspect raw Event ID 13 XML from machine and user hives. Verify `EventType`, `TargetObject`, `Image`, `ProcessGuid`, `ProcessId`, `User`, `Details`, `EventRecordID`, Computer, provider, and channel. Test a value type whose Details is populated and one whose behavior is not guaranteed. Protect paths, users, and command/value data with least-privilege search roles.

## Step 2 — Prove source and field health separately

Maintain an expected-endpoint ledger with stable endpoint ID, role, owner, Sysmon/config hash, collection route, enabled time, and retirement time. Source-health searches must detect no recurring Sysmon telemetry, stopped service, Event ID 16 drift, Event ID 255 errors, wrong source/type/provider/channel, excessive `_indextime-_time`, clock skew, duplicate routes, record replay, and extraction loss for TargetObject/EventType/Image/ProcessGuid/User/EventRecordID. Event ID 13 can be rare; use recurring qualified Sysmon event families or deployment telemetry as the heartbeat. Never convert no Run-key events into “no Run keys.”

Profile coverage requires separate evidence. A loaded user's current-user hive appears under `HKU\<SID>`; offline profiles and writes before collection are not reconstructed by Event ID 13. Where baseline assurance matters, run a separately governed read-only current-state inventory and compare it with approved values. State inventory and change telemetry answer different questions.

## Step 3 — Save, schedule, and understand the SPL

Save the sidecar SPL as `windows_sysmon_run_runonce_value_sets`. Schedule every five minutes with `earliest=-10m@m latest=-5m@m`, evaluating one complete five-minute slice after a fixed five-minute indexing allowance. Measure p99 direct/WEC delay and update schedule plus fixtures together if this is insufficient. Trigger when result count exceeds zero. Group notification only by exact endpoint, full key, value name, and bounded time; preserve every EventRecordID.

The base clause fixes index, XML source type, exact Sysmon channel source, EventCode, and closed time. The first `eval` normalizes endpoint and EventType and retains missing optional evidence as `unknown`. The next expressions split final value name from TargetObject, classify only `HKLM` or `HKU\SID`, remove that root on a lowercase comparison copy, and permit exactly four relative keys. This avoids false scope from broad `*CurrentVersion\Run*` matching. Original key spelling remains in output. Event and indexed times make latency visible.

Do not restore the old `NOT match(Details,"program files|system32|syswow64")` filter. Legitimate directories can host abused signed binaries, malicious values can reference other locations indirectly, and `Details` may be absent. Path reputation is triage context, not a safe base-search exclusion. Do not call every AppData/Temp command malware. Also do not merge Event IDs 12/14: they represent key/value create-delete or rename semantics, not this value-set contract.

The optional CIM SPL follows Splunk Security Content's `Endpoint.Registry` approach. Before use, prove raw-to-normalized parity for action, destination, process, hive/path, value name/data/type, user, and vendor product, then validate acceleration range/lag. Other EDR vendors can populate the dataset. Keep raw Event ID 13 and XML authoritative.

## Step 4 — Validate paths, fields, timing, and exceptions

Use fixed-time isolated fixtures from the qualified Sysmon/add-on pair. Run both control scenarios and assert every output field. Add positives for native/32-bit machine/user Run and RunOnce, mixed root/path case, Unicode value names, spaces and quotes, blank Details, and long values. Add negatives for prefix/suffix lookalikes, `RunServices`, `Policies\Explorer\Run`, `StartupApproved`, Event IDs 12/14, wrong channel/source type/provider/index, missing endpoint/value name, and both dispatch boundaries. Test late indexing, clock skew, duplicate local/WEC collection, EventRecordID replay, and multiple rapid writes without accidental deduplication.

On a disposable lab endpoint/profile, create and then modify a harmless test value using an approved `reg.exe` or PowerShell procedure; do not point it to an untrusted executable and do not alter production autostart solely for testing. Compare Event Viewer **Details > XML View**, raw Splunk XML, output fields, and current state from `reg query` or `Get-ItemProperty`. Remove the value, verify cleanup, and retain exact command, operator, configuration hash, times, record IDs, search job, and expected/actual results. A removed current value does not invalidate the historical event.

Test notification exceptions after base results: exact match, expiry boundary, malformed time, changed value/process, wildcard rejection, evidence preservation, and continued source-health alerting. Keep `status=draft` until endpoint/profile coverage, source health, field extraction, raw/CIM parity if used, fixtures, schedule, alert delivery, dashboard, exception policy, response, and cleanup are accepted by Windows, endpoint-security, software, and Splunk owners.

## Step 5 — Triage and respond without overclaiming

Place source health above activity counts. Alert text should say “Run/RunOnce value set observed,” not “persistence confirmed.” Include endpoint/role, scope, full key/value, observed Details with its limitation, writer image/GUID/PID/user, event/index times, record ID, prevalence, software/change context, exception status, and runbook.

Responder sequence:
1. Verify source, raw XML, EventCode/EventType, endpoint, event/index time, record ID, extraction, and collection-route uniqueness.
2. Resolve machine versus user SID/profile and 32/64-bit view; query the exact current value read-only and preserve it before change.
3. Correlate ProcessGuid with Sysmon process creation, parent/command line, signer/hash, logon, EDR, file/network activity, and software-deployment records.
4. Compare exact key/value/data/process with approved baseline, owner, package/version, policy/job, ticket, endpoint role, and prevalence.
5. Determine later execution from separate sign-in/process evidence; Event ID 13 alone cannot establish it.
6. If suspicious, follow approved endpoint containment/scoping and preserve evidence before deleting a value or file. If authorized, document exact content and use only a bounded exception.
7. Verify intended current state, no unauthorized recreation, source health, exception expiry, and retained disposition before closure.

Prioritize unexpected user-writable paths, interpreters/encoded commands, unsigned or rare writers, mismatched user/process, fleet spread, recreation after removal, and correlated compromise—but calculate severity downstream. Never automatically delete values, kill processes, disable accounts, or isolate hosts from this neutral change event; legitimate startup software can be business-critical.

## Step 6 — Troubleshoot product-specific failures

- **No Event ID 13 for a controlled write:** verify Sysmon service/version, active configuration/schema, RegistryEvent include path and rule relation, Event IDs 16/255, local Operational channel, and exact registry view/profile.
- **Event exists locally but not Splunk:** inspect WinEventLog stanza deployment, XML rendering, forwarder queues/checkpoint, index routing/RBAC, source/type, WEC subscription, and dispatch time.
- **TargetObject or process fields are null:** inspect raw EventData names, Sysmon/add-on versions and placement, source identity, and conflicting props/transforms. Retain field-quality failure; do not suppress broadly.
- **Details is blank or incomplete:** respect Microsoft's documented DWORD/QWORD guarantee; query current state and correlate qualified telemetry. Never invent a command or drop the event.
- **HKCU test is missing:** map the test user to loaded `HKU\SID`, verify the write occurred in that hive and the include condition covers it. Offline profiles are not live event sources.
- **Adjacent keys appear:** inspect local SPL edits and normalized `relative_key`; the supplied exact `IN` list excludes RunServices, Policies, and StartupApproved.
- **Duplicate rows:** distinguish direct plus WEC ingestion or checkpoint replay from two real writes using Computer/channel/EventRecordID/raw hash/index time. Repair routing instead of broad `dedup`.
- **CIM results differ:** verify Endpoint.Registry tags, add-on/CIM versions, acceleration range/lag, summaries-only behavior, vendor data, and exact path normalization. Keep raw results authoritative.
- **Volume spikes during rollout:** match exact package, values, writers, target ring, and change window. Use narrow expiring notification exceptions; never filter the registry event at ingestion without security-owner review.
grandmaExplanation: We watch the Windows list of programs that can start when someone signs in. A change may come from a normal installer or from an unwanted program, so we keep the exact change and ask who made it and why.
